name: יְהוֹרָם
summary: Two kings of the same years bore it, written both יְהוֹרָם and יוֹרָם: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, who married Athaliah daughter of Ahab and walked in the way of the kings of Israel (2Ki 8:16–18; 2Ch 21:1–6), in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat 1:8, Ἰωράμ); and Jehoram son of Ahab, king of Israel, wounded at Ramoth-gilead and shot by Jehu (2Ki 3:1; 8:28–29; 9:24). Also a priest sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law in Judah (2Ch 17:8), Joram son of Toi king of Hamath, sent to greet David (2Sa 8:10; Hadoram in 1Ch 18:10), and a Levite of the treasuries (1Ch 26:25). The name is יְהוֹ “Yahweh” with רָם “high, exalted”: “Yahweh is exalted”, as the psalms say, “exalted be the God of my salvation” (Psa 18:47).

evidence.note: “Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign”, in the fifth year of יוֹרָם son of Ahab.
“יְהוֹרָם the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria.”
With Elishama, “Jehoram the priests”, who taught in Judah with the book of the law.
“Toi sent יוֹרָם his son to King David.”
“Yahweh lives … וְיָרוּם the God of my salvation.”

note: BDB's e.az.aw (49 tokens) counts both spellings; e.az.bx (יוֹרָם, a cross-reference) has none and is not listed. The first element belongs to the yahweh name entry; the name is filed under its second element, as jehoshaphat is under shaphat. Hadoram (1Ch 18:10) is a different name borne by Toi's son and is not claimed. The two kings' reigns overlap and both names appear in the same verses (2Ki 8:16, 25), so the reader must follow the father's name.
